info.title: Traceway
info.description: One API. A call returns the signed-in person's own data, or a course opened with a signed link. There is no list of other people. A password, two-factor secret, recovery code, or remember token is never returned.

post.summary: Send a saved route to a connected service
post.description: Wahoo syncs the route to the ELEMNT. Ride with GPS keeps it in the library, and the rider sends it on from there with Send to Device, for a Karoo or Bryton. A second send replaces the first copy.

200.description: The route is at the service, or the service is still reading it.

url.description: The route at the service, when it has a page.

409.description: The service is not connected, or it needs connecting again.

502.description: The service did not take the route just now.

delete.summary: Disconnect an account at another service
delete.description: Traceway asks the service to withdraw the keys it gave, when it holds any, then forgets the connection and the routes sent through it. A rider cannot disconnect their last way to log in.

302.description: Back to Connections, with what happened.

404.description: Traceway does not know that service.

RouteDetails.description: How a route climbs, what it runs on, where it turns, and where to stop.

profile.description: Pairs of metres from the start and the height of the ground in metres.

Error.description: A call that did not succeed. A validation failure also lists one message per field.

errors.description: Present when a field failed validation. The key is the field name.

last_seen_at.description: The last time the rider was signed in and using Traceway, to the quarter hour.

pending_email.description: A new email the rider asked for, waiting for them to open the link sent to it.

admin_actions.description: What the people who run Traceway did to this account, and when. Kept for a year.

connections.description: The accounts at other services the rider connected, to log in with or send routes to. The keys any of them gave are withheld.

account_number.description: The service's own number for the rider's account there.

account.description: The email or username the service shared, where Traceway may keep it.

allowed.description: What the rider allowed Traceway to do, as the service names it.

sent.description: Each saved route, or leg, sent to the service. Leg 0 is the whole route.

shape.description: How the route goes: a loop, out and back, one way, or along points the rider drew. Null for a multisport plan.

image_url.description: The picture chats show for the link: the route on the map, 1200 by 630.

details.description: The climb, surfaces, turns, and stops. Null for a multisport plan or a route saved before they were read.

legs.description: The legs of a multisport plan, in order. Empty for a single sport.

color.description: The colour picked for the leg, as #rrggbb.

details.description: The climb, surfaces, turns, and stops of a land leg. Null for the swim or a plan saved before they were read.

BuildRouteRequest.description: The points to join, and how the roads should be chosen.

ClaimDevicePairingRequest.description: The secret the device got when it opened the pairing.

ExportFitCourseRequest.description: The course to write into a FIT file.

leg.description: The leg of a multisport plan. The course is named after it, such as "Brick 2 Run".

ImportRouteRequest.description: A GPX file to plan from.

file.description: A .gpx file of at most 5 MB.

PreviewMultisportRequest.description: The transition, an optional swim, and the land legs in order.

stretch.description: A chained leg covers distance_metres on the way to its finish, rather than taking the shortest way.

PreviewRouteRequest.description: The pin, the sport, and the length.

RedoImportedRouteRequest.description: An imported line and how to ride it again.

mode.description: keep the line, reverse it, or start it from the pin.

name.description: The name read from the file.

SearchPlacesRequest.description: What a rider typed, and the middle of the map they look at.

SendRouteToServiceRequest.description: Which part of the route to send. Leave out the leg for a single-sport route.

leg.description: A land leg of a multisport plan, counted from 1.

LinkDeviceRequest.description: The code on the device and a name for it.

code.description: Six letters and digits. Spaces and case do not matter.

PasswordUpdateRequest.description: The current password and the replacement. Neither is returned. A rider who signed up with a connected account and has no password yet sets one without the current password, since the page already asked them to confirm it is them.

ProfileDeleteRequest.description: Confirms the deletion. The password is not returned. A rider without a password confirms it is them with a passkey or a connected account first, and sends none.

password.description: Confirms the deletion. It is not stored in the response.

ProfileUpdateRequest.description: The name and email of the signed-in person. A new email waits until the link sent to it is opened, and asking for one needs the current password, or a confirmation a moment ago for an account without one.

current_password.description: Needed to ask for a new email, unless the rider confirmed it is them a moment ago. It is not returned.

SnapPointRequest.description: A point, and the sport and surface used to choose a road or a path.

surface.description: The route's surface. Without it, the sport's own.

StartDevicePairingRequest.description: The device app that asks for a code.

StoreRouteImageRequest.description: The picture a shared link shows: the route on the map.

image.description: A JPEG of 1200 by 630, at most 1 MB.

StoreSavedRouteRequest.description: The route the signed-in person wants to keep.

layout.description: How the legs of a multisport plan meet.

legs.description: The legs of a multisport plan, in order. The swim, if any, comes first.

color.description: The colour picked for the leg, as #rrggbb.

session.description: The session cookie of the signed-in person. State-changing calls also send the X-XSRF-TOKEN header. A signed share link does not use this cookie.
session.name: laravel_session

deviceToken.description: The token a device app, such as Traceway for Connect IQ on a Garmin, gets after the rider types its pairing code in Settings, then Devices. It reads only that rider's own routes.
